_readme: Machine-readable copy of CONTEXT.md sections 4, 5 and the verbatim copy. The engine and the web app read from this file. No screen or module hard-codes a number or a legal sentence. If this file and CONTEXT.md disagree, fix one of them and note it in the worklog. source values: published, back-test, simulation, assumption, contract, formula, plan.

product.name: Rehat
product.payment: PayNow to the company UEN by the 5th working day of next month

heat.meter: Hourly mean of the four 15-minute WBGT readings at the named station

tiers.label: MOM: at least 10 minutes rest an hour for heavy work (mandatory)
MOM framework sets 15 minutes an hour

rain.meter: Clock-hour rainfall total at the named rain gauge

haze.meter: NEA 24-hour PSI for the region at 12:00

fallback_ladder: Labelled model estimate, sent for review
After 14 days: settle at the published regional advisory level
retired: Site Match as a core plan option

levers.plain: The monthly allowance. A normal month, plus a buffer, stays with the firm.
We pay S$8 against a cost of about S$10.20 an hour, so the firm keeps about a fifth.
60 insured hours a year, S$480 a worker.

rate_lock_years.note: The lock itself is not priced yet

renewal_discount.note: For a full-year break log and no MOM heat action. To be tested in the pilot

expected_insured_hours_year.basis: 26-year observed back-test (8.78 h) plus 1.0 h haze load assumption

expected_payout_year.basis: Observed pricing back-test with haze load assumption

premium_split.label: Reinsurance
premium_split.note: From year 2. Income keeps the pilot's risk

premium_split.label: Profit
premium_split.note: 15% in the pilot year, because no reinsurance is bought

three_year_path.note: Year 2 profit dips because reinsurance starts

haze_stress_scenario.label: 2015-style haze stress
haze_stress_scenario.basis: Published capital-stress scenario for a severe 2015-style haze year. It is not an observed recovery result and never changes a customer payout or price.

stress_tests.stress: Heat up 30%, rain up 10%, normals not reset

all_crews.note: MOM work permit holders in construction, shipyard and process, Jun 2026, x S$129. Includes large firms, which are later

reachable_first.note: 25% of small firms. Open question 1 in CONTEXT.md

facts.text: Days of high heat stress: 37 in 2023, 21 in 2024, 29 in 2025
MOM has taken enforcement action against 213 employers
About a third of 250 workplaces inspected in the hotter months of 2024 breached heat rules
Four more heat measures are mandatory from 1 Dec 2026
Work permit holders must be paid the declared salary even when there is no work
About two-thirds of normal downtime hours are heavy rain

worked_month.note: Heat from real sampled readings. Rain and normals are assumptions. The engine test for this month must produce S$510.

demo_clock.note: Offline demo mode pins one date so every screen agrees. Default is May 2026. Tanjong Greenworks' May receipt has 11.5 rain hours against a 7.44-hour deductible and pays S$650 on 8 June. The S$510 worked month is a Bishan test fixture; the demo firm's own figure comes from the engine. Keep the 31 October 2025 replay and its zero-payment receipt for questions.

copy.tagline: Rest that is paid for gets taken.
copy.hook: At a heat reading of 32, a contractor pays for 60 minutes and gets 50.
copy.human_line: A normal month is part of the job. A hard month, we carry with you.
copy.one_line: One tick box on the work injury policy. No claim form.
copy.may_not_pay: Rehat pays only when NEA's published readings at your named station cross the levels shown; your own site can be hotter or wetter than the station, so you can lose work time and receive nothing.
copy.employer_sms: Rehat pays $8/worker/hr when NEA heat (WBGT 32+), heavy rain or haze at your station runs above a normal month. Station only: you may lose time and get $0.
copy.warranty: We give the rest breaks MOM requires and do not cut pay for them.
copy.worker_notice_en: WBGT is 32 now. You get 10 minutes of rest in shade every hour. Your pay is not cut. No break? Scan to tell us.
copy.heat_alert: Heat reading is 32 at {station}. Ten-minute breaks start now.
copy.forecast_alert: Heat stress likely {from} to {to} tomorrow at {station}. Plan heavy work early.
copy.rule_statement: At a heat reading (WBGT) of 32 or more, MOM requires at least 10 minutes of rest every hour for heavy work. MOM's framework sets 15 minutes at 33.

teach_back_options.text: When NEA's readings at my named station run above a normal month
Whenever my own site is too hot or too wet to work
Whenever I send in a claim form

copy.teach_back_explain: Rehat reads NEA's station, not your site, and there is no claim form. If the station's month is normal, Rehat pays nothing.
copy.footer: Concept prototype for Income Insurance, Singapore-India Hackathon 2026. Not an Income product. Fictional data.
copy.legal_status: Designed to be confirmed by Income's legal team
copy.ask: Would you pilot this? And if not, what would have to be true?
never_say: The employer pays one-fourth of the wage

glossary.plain: Wet bulb globe temperature. NEA's measure of heat stress. It combines temperature, humidity, wind and sun.
The NEA weather station named on your policy. Rehat pays on its readings, not on your site.
The downtime your station usually sees in that calendar month. It is reset every year.
The part you carry: a normal month plus your plan's buffer.
An hour of downtime above your deductible. Rehat pays S$8 per outdoor worker for it.
Rehat pays S$8 of an hour that costs you about S$10.20. You keep the rest.
The most Rehat pays: 20 insured hours a month and 60 a year, S$480 a worker.
NEA's data for that hour is missing or late. We wait for it. We never count missing data as zero.
An hourly record of the heat reading and the rest owed. You can show it to an MOM inspector.
The share of premium paid back to customers as claims. Rehat targets 65%.
Reinsurance that pays Income when a year's claims pass 150% of premium.
NEA's 24-hour air quality index. Above 100 is unhealthy.
